summary:
Turn 19 delivered the map handoff for the now-confirmed recovery finding, so the understanding layer matches the three reviewed checks instead of lagging behind them.

State on entry. All three current artifacts for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector are confirmed in scope with no_issue_found correspondence: the resolution does not adopt a reply reporting the instance COMMITTED (adopted_committed false), the accept round it starts nevertheless completes (accept_oks 0 to 1) and commits a NOOP vector for that instance (vectors_match false), and after the recoverer's Commit broadcast the disagreement survives across replicas (all_committed_match false, replica1 keeps PUT while replica0 and replica2 hold NOOP).

Map update (accepted base version 4, three clarified objects). Behavior B9 gained a sourced branch stating that the recovering replica sets its own bal and vbal to the newly made ballot before building its PrepareReply, so its own entry announces the new ballot as its VBallot while the leader bookkeeping was seeded with the record's old vbal; its unknown asking whether the local record is a sufficient seed is replaced by the honest residual (the checks fix the resolution and accept rounds; the execution-timeout trigger and a real commit round are unread). Behavior B11 gained the described effect of the selection rule, namely that the candidate is the last reply at or above the running maximum and that the self entry has already raised that maximum above older remote values, with the confirmed observation attached. core_overview's context explanation now carries the sourced conditional relationship instead of an intent-only description: the own-vbal raise, the skipped older remote values, the confirmed NOOP-versus-committed divergence and the fact that the Commit broadcast does not repair it. Each change has a map_changes entry with sources and a preserves explanation; no requirement, binding, edge or identity moved, and the claim plus its checks remain the home for the verdict.

Remaining discriminator kept visible in feedback: whether executing the instances makes the disagreement visible in applied state (the checks compare records, not state machines), whether the timeout trigger and a real commit round reach the same state, and whether the accept-phase status omission changes the same recovery decision. The paused accept-status candidate is still available for that last item, and no earlier result, premise or observation was weakened.
